title: The Guy Who Studies Too
description:
Two in the morning, the goshiwon's shared kitchen. {name} followed the sound of boiling water and found Hyunsu.

An exam book lay face-down next to the pot. Administrative law. Its corners were so worn the paper had gone soft as cloth.

"You prepping for something too, hyung?"

Four years into the Grade 9 civil service exam, he said. This year was his last shot. Even as he said it, he watched the noodles through their full three minutes. The posture of a man who has learned how to wait.

His face was tired, but it wasn't the face of someone who had given up.

choices.text: Encourage him
choices.result_text:
"You'll get it this year."

There was nothing to back it up. Hyunsu grinned anyway. A real one.
"You'll be fine too, hyung."

Back in his room, lying down, {name} found the words stayed longer than expected. Two baseless sentences traded in a kitchen at dawn — and somehow they held.

choices.text: "Four years is a long time"
choices.result_text:
"Yeah, it has." Hyunsu said it while setting the pot down. "But quitting now feels like I'd regret it even longer."

{name} understood that.
Choosing a different path versus staying on this one — you only find out which was right later.

While the broth went cold, the two of them quietly went on with their separate arithmetic.

title: Exam Day
description:
Five in the morning — {name} half-woke to the sound of a door closing.

Footsteps faded down the hall. Hyunsu. Today was the exam. Grade 9 administrative track — four years graded in a single day.

He closed his eyes again, and when they wouldn't stay closed, stared at the ceiling. Out in the shared kitchen, a single cup sat upturned at Hyunsu's spot. Washed and left to dry. A man who washes his cup even on the dawn he leaves for the exam.

What kind of evening he would come home to — nobody knew yet.

choices.text: Ask how it went later
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu came back late in the evening. The sound of him taking off his shoes was slower than it had been that morning.

"How'd it go?"

He paused before answering.
"I think it went okay. Maybe."

Maybe. The most honest word available to a man who had bet four years. {name} didn't ask anything else and put water on for ramyeon. That night, {name} did the cooking.

choices.text: Say nothing — better not to press
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu came back quietly in the evening. His door closed more slowly than usual.

When they passed in the hallway, {name} asked with his eyes only. Hyunsu gave a small nod. Whether it signaled that he was okay, or that he wanted to be — there was no telling.

That night the light in Hyunsu's room stayed on late. The unofficial answer key would already be up online by then.

title: Hyunsu Passed
description:
Hyunsu sent a message: "Hyung, could you come by my room for a minute?" {name} walked down the corridor of Hyunsu's goshiwon and stopped at his door. When it opened, Hyunsu spoke.

"Hyung, I passed."

He said it quietly. No shouting, no smile. His phone was still in his hand, the acceptance screen glowing, his fingertips pressed white against the glass.

Four years. Every year he failed, he had turned one year older and opened the same workbook again — and all of that time was pressed into that one low voice.

"I wanted to tell you first, hyung."

choices.text: Congratulate him
choices.result_text:
"Wait, seriously? For real?"

{name}'s voice got loud first. Only then did Hyunsu smile. A kind of smile {name} hadn't seen before — the kind that comes out when what's been held in finally gives way.

He clapped Hyunsu's shoulder awkwardly in the narrow hallway. The 2 AM ramyeon, the washed cup left to dry, the worn administrative law book. All of it had been leading to today.

{name} felt good, as if it were his own.
When someone else's success brings this much joy — maybe that's the sign of a real connection.

title: Hyunsu Didn't Pass
description:
On Monday, when the result was posted, one Kakao message arrived from Hyunsu.

“Hyung, I didn't pass.”

For the next three days, Hyunsu did not leave his room. The sound of ramyeon water boiling disappeared from the shared kitchen. {name} went to Hyunsu's goshiwon with a convenience-store bag. Only light leaked from under the door.

Should he knock? He raised his hand, lowered it, then raised it again.

description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_exam_e: Standing at the door, {name} remembers the problem photo they reviewed over Kakao on the final Sunday before the exam. Hyunsu had said he would finish that one problem and sleep.
Standing at the door, {name} remembers Hyunsu's reply from the final Sunday before the exam: “Okay. I'll set my alarm and lie down. You sleep too, hyung.”
description_memory_if_known.future_story_source:hyunsu_exam_2026:hyu: On the final Sunday before the exam, {name} did not answer Hyunsu's Kakao message. Standing outside the door now, he remembers the problem photo that remained on the screen that night.

choices.text: Knock on the door
choices.result_text:
After a long while, the door opened.

Hyunsu's eyes were swollen. An open workbook lay on the floor.

{name} took two drinks out of the bag and held one out. Hyunsu took it. The sound of the can opening rang strangely loud in the small room.

They sat without speaking until both cans were empty.

choices.text: Leave him be — he probably wants to be alone
choices.result_text:
{name} left without knocking, still carrying the convenience-store bag.

On the fourth day, he visited the goshiwon again and found Hyunsu washing his face for a long time at the shared sink. When the water stopped, their eyes met in the hallway. Hyunsu gave a small nod.

{name} nodded back. He asked nothing that day.

title: Three Notifications on One Screen
description:
At 5:42 on Friday afternoon, a text came from the broker. "The lease is signed and the deposit is confirmed. We'll hand you the key on the agreed date." Two minutes later, a message from Hyunsu covered the screen where the money for the new room had gone.

"Hyung, I didn't pass."

Then came a request to cover a paid shift that weekend. The reply was due at six. {name} looked at the amount once and sent, "I can't do this weekend."

By night, there was no sound from the shared kitchen or Hyunsu's room. Carrying a convenience-store bag with two drinks, {name} stopped outside the door at the end of the hall. Only a thin line of desk-lamp light slipped underneath, falling across an exam book inside. The deposit, Hyunsu's message, and the shift he had given up still shared one phone screen.

description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_exam_e: Before turning down the weekend shift, {name} reopened the problem photo they had reviewed on the final Sunday before the exam. Hyunsu had said he would finish that one problem and sleep.

Before turning down the weekend shift, {name} remembered Hyunsu's answer the night before the exam: "I'll set my alarm and lie down. You sleep too, hyung." Today's failure message sat directly below it.
description_memory_if_known.future_story_source:hyunsu_exam_2026:hyu: On the final Sunday before the exam, {name} had not answered Hyunsu's problem photo. Today, in place of that unanswered night, the first thing he sent was a refusal of the weekend shift.

choices.text: Knock, then wait until he answers
choices.result_text:
Only after the third knock did footsteps move inside. Hyunsu opened the door a hand's width. His eyes were swollen, and the exam book on the floor still lay open to the page he had studied.

{name} prepared no consolation. He only took one drink from the bag. Hyunsu opened the door a little farther and accepted it.

"Aren't you going to say anything, hyung?"
"I didn't come to find the right words today."

The two cans opened almost together. Neither of them mentioned the next exam after that sound.

choices.text: Hang the bag on the handle and text that he does not have to answer
choices.result_text:
{name} did not knock. He looped the bag over the door handle and sent a message. "I left this outside. You don't have to answer. Be alone tonight."

The unread mark remained as the screen went dark. {name} walked down the stairs. His phone buzzed once when he reached the floor below, but he did not take it out.

At the end of the hall, only the closed door and the white handles of the convenience-store bag remained.

title: The Empty Cup Space
description:
At 11:18 on Friday night, after {name} transferred the first rent for his new room, Hyunsu sent a photo. It showed the shelf in their old goshiwon's shared kitchen. The square where {name}'s cup used to sit was empty. Hyunsu's face appeared nowhere in the image.

"It feels strange without your cup, hyung. Does the new place feel like somewhere a person can live?"

Three minutes later, another bubble appeared. "I still haven't closed the box with my exam books. I don't know what I'll do yet, either. You don't have to answer."

{name} sat against the floor of the new room and watched the screen. There was traffic outside the window, but no sound of ramyeon water boiling next door. Above the reply box remained the final exchange from the day Hyunsu said he had failed. Hyunsu had not come to this room. All that lay between them now was one photo and a blinking cursor.

choices.text: Send a photo of the new room and admit he is still adjusting too
choices.result_text:
{name} framed the unpacked boxes and his cup on the floor in one shot. "I don't know if it's fit for a person yet. I'm making it into somewhere I can live. I don't know yet either."

After the sent mark appeared, Hyunsu's three typing dots came and went. A moment later, one line arrived: "It looks like your room, hyung." The two photos sat one above the other in the chat.

choices.text: Instead of offering a solution, ask whether he ate today
choices.result_text:
"You can close the box tomorrow. What did you eat today?"

The answer came quickly. "Ramyeon. The water boiled over, so I cleaned the kitchen."

{name} sent one laughing icon. The conversation continued for a few more lines without mentioning careers or exams. Hyunsu's last bubble read, "You should eat something too, hyung."

choices.text: Say he cannot write properly now, and give a time for tomorrow's reply
choices.result_text:
Instead of the advice he had typed and erased, {name} sent, "I can't answer this properly now. I'll write again tomorrow at ten in the morning."

The unread mark vanished at once, but no reply came. {name} put Hyunsu's name in the alarm title. After the screen locked, the number 10 A.M. stayed in his head.

title: Hyunsu's New Direction
description:
Hyunsu called and said, "I'm packing. Could you come by for a minute?" {name} went to Hyunsu's goshiwon. Hyunsu stopped packing long enough to open the door.

He was done with the civil service exam, he said. He'd prepare for a job instead. His major had been accounting; he'd start over on that road.

Inside the box, four years of exam books were stacked in neat rows. He wasn't throwing them out — he was packing them. "If I sell them used, the next person can use them." One by one, Hyunsu laid the worn-cornered books in straight.

"It's not farther, and it's not closer. It's just a different road."

{name} turned those words over for a long time. It was a sentence you could hold up against your own road, too.

choices.text: Tell him it'll work out
choices.result_text:
"You'll do great."

Hyunsu smiled. A firmer smile this time. Not the face of a man folding up four years — the face of a man starting something.

The last thing into the box was the calendar, the exam date still circled on it. Hyunsu didn't throw that away.

Choosing a different road and giving up are not the same thing.
{name} learned that from Hyunsu.

title: A Message from Hyunsu
description:
That evening, his phone gave a short buzz. Hyunsu.

"Hyung, I got hired at an accounting firm."

A photo followed. Hyunsu in a navy suit, holding a new business card. The awkward angle and smile made it obvious someone else had told him to pose.

{name}'s finger stopped over the reply box. Congratulations was easy. There was something else he wanted to look at first.

choices.text: Look at Hyunsu's face before the card
choices.result_text: He zoomed in. Before the crisp business card, he saw the same awkward smile above it.

choices.text: Remember the days outside his door before the new job
choices.result_text: Instead of congratulations, he typed the first line about the day neither of them had forgotten.

title: The Face in the Photo
description:
The print on the card was too small to read. What he could see was the slight lift in Hyunsu's shoulders and the way one cheek rose first when he smiled. The same face that used to wait for ramyeon in the goshiwon kitchen.

{name}: "Who took that angle?"
Hyunsu: "The youngest guy at the office. He took more than ten. Said this was the best one."

Four years of failing, folding, and beginning again — and Hyunsu was still Hyunsu. The fact felt unexpectedly good.

choices.text: Ask him to eat in the old neighborhood this weekend
choices.result_text:
The reply arrived the moment the read receipt appeared.
"Sounds good. I'll get there first."

title: At the Door on the Third Day
description:
{name}: "I'm sorry I couldn't say anything outside your door back then."

A reply came after a pause.
Hyunsu: "I heard the convenience-store bag rustling outside. And that you didn't knock. Back then, that helped."

For years, whether leaving him alone had been neglect or patience stayed unclear. At least Hyunsu had carried his own answer.

description_if_known.hyunsu_comforted:
{name}: "Remember when I knocked on your door?"

The reply came at once.
Hyunsu: "Even the sound of the cans opening. That was the loudest thing I heard that day."

{name} watched the screen for a while. What had been only two drinks to him had remained, for someone else, as the day he opened the door again.

choices.text: Ask him to eat in the old neighborhood this weekend
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu did not need to ask where.
"That gukbap place, right? See you Saturday, hyung."

title: Hyunsu, Again
description:
On Saturday evening, Hyunsu was already waiting at a gukbap place in the alley by their old goshiwon. He wore the navy suit from the photo, though he had unbuttoned the jacket.

Hyunsu: "Hyung. It really has been a while."
{name}: "You look better than the photo."
Hyunsu: "Or was the photo just that bad?"

They laughed. Before the food arrived, Hyunsu slid a new business card across the table. The crisp edge stopped against a water glass.

Hyunsu: "I wanted you to have the first one."

choices.text: Congratulate him for everything he endured
choices.result_text:
"You really did it. Starting over and all of it."

Hyunsu lowered his head, then smiled instead of answering. The same smile from the days they waited for ramyeon water.

In Seoul, there were evenings like this. Some left a deposit that never appeared in an account, but remained all the same.

choices.text: "From now on, let's be the first to call when things get hard"
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu's eyes widened for a moment.
"You're really saying that first, hyung?"

They laughed and took out their phones. It took only seconds to confirm numbers already saved. The promise was not the number. It was who could press it first.

title: Hyunsu's Posting
description:
Hyunsu shared the posting news and asked {name} to visit the room one last time. {name} went to Hyunsu's goshiwon. When he opened the door, Hyunsu was packing boxes.

"Hyung, I got my posting. I have to go next week."

Some county office in Gyeonggi-do. Four years living in this room, and it came to two boxes. One box of exam books, one box of everything else. The calendar sat on top — the circle drawn around the exam date still sharp.

With his door propped open, Hyunsu tore off a strip of tape. The rasp of it carried down the hall.

Four years in this room, packed into two boxes. Whatever didn't fit — that probably goes with him, written into the body.

choices.text: Buy him dinner
choices.result_text:
A sundae gukbap place nearby. Hyunsu ate a lot. The meal of a man with no exam tomorrow.

"When are you getting out of here, hyung?"
"...Not sure yet."

Instead of answering further, {name} pushed the dish of radish kimchi toward him. Hyunsu didn't press; he just smiled. That smile stayed a long time.

Same starting line — and one of them had left first. Picking up the bill, {name} thought: strangely, he didn't begrudge this money at all.

choices.text: Tell him it's great news. Say goodbye.
choices.result_text:
"Good for you. Take care of yourself out there."
"Thank you, hyung."

No handshake, no hug. The goshiwon hallway was too narrow for that, and the two of them too unpracticed at it.

The room was empty the next day. The shared kitchen, one ramyeon pot missing, looked strangely bigger than before.

For a few days, the absence of boiling water at two in the morning felt wrong.

title: Someone Who Settled In
description:
Hyunsu reached out after a long while.

A photo. Hyunsu laughing at a work dinner. A suit. Coworkers.

"Hyung, you good? I've kind of found my footing now."

{name} looked at the photo for a long time.

Four years ago they were eating cup ramyeon in the same goshiwon. Hyunsu found his place. {name} is still — running.

description_if_known.hyunsu_passed:
Hyunsu reached out after a long while.

A photo. In front of a county office. Hyunsu, name tag on, smiling awkwardly.

"Hyung, I'm a public officer now. All settled in."

{name} looked at the photo for a long time.

Four years ago they were eating cup ramyeon in the same goshiwon. Hyunsu crossed the starting line first. {name} is still — running.

choices.text: Say it honestly — "I'm a little jealous"
choices.result_text:
"Come on, hyung, why?" Hyunsu laughed.

What he envied was the stability. A road with a fixed end. {name}'s road still had no end in sight. Which left only one option: keep going.

choices.text: Just congratulate him — and turn back to the screen
choices.result_text:
"Congrats. Really, that's great."

He set the phone down and went back to the investment screen. No time to envy. One year left.

title: A Call at the End of Five Years
description:
The home stretch. Gangnam was genuinely close now.

Hyunsu called. Video call.

"Hyung! It's been forever. How are you?"

Behind Hyunsu on the screen were office fluorescents and stacks of paperwork. Working late, apparently, but his face was at ease. The face of someone settled into his own life. When somebody called him mid-conversation, even his "Yes, one minute" carried no strain at all.

{name} looked at his own face in the corner of the screen. Five years were in it.

He decided not to measure who had come farther. They had never been walking the same map.

description_if_known.crossed_line:
The home stretch. Gangnam was genuinely close now.

Hyunsu called. Video call.

"Hyung! It's been forever. How are you?"

Hyunsu was smiling, glad to see him, but {name} found it strangely hard to look straight at the screen. His eyes kept drifting to his own face in the corner.

The guy he'd shared cup ramyeon with in that dawn kitchen five years ago — what would he say if he saw who {name} was now?

"Hyung? Can you not hear me?"
"No — no, I hear you."

He heard him fine. That was the problem — he heard him too well.
description_if_known.father_passed:
The home stretch. Gangnam was genuinely close now.

Hyunsu called. Video call.

"Hyung! It's been forever. How's your father—"

Hyunsu stopped. Apparently some things carry even across a screen. {name} hadn't said a word, and Hyunsu didn't ask.

A short silence passed. Not the silence of choosing words of comfort — the silence of deciding not to.

"...Hyung, make sure you eat."

That was all he said. It stayed longer than anything else {name} heard that day.
description_if_known.called_hyunsu_first:
The home stretch. Gangnam was genuinely close now.

Hyunsu called. Video call.

"Hyung! It's been forever. How are you?"

Behind Hyunsu on the screen were office fluorescents and stacks of paperwork. Working late, apparently, but his face was at ease. The face of someone settled into his own life.

{name} looked at his own face in the corner of the screen. Five years were in it.

A number he had once dialed first, for no reason at all. To have one number you can call without needing a reason — since that day, this call has never once felt awkward.

choices.text: Say it for real — "I made it because of you"
choices.result_text:
"What are you talking about, hyung, you did all of it."

He hadn't. It was because someone had held on beside him in that 2 AM kitchen that he didn't fold halfway. Enduring alone and enduring with someone in the next room are different things.

He never quite got the whole thing out. Only after hanging up did the unsaid part linger in the room, a long while.

choices.text: "I'll have good news soon" — hang up with a smile
choices.result_text:
"I'll be waiting, hyung!"

He ended the call. When the screen went dark, the room grew one shade quieter.

Soon. Really, soon. {name} sat back down at the desk. For a moment, the face reflected in the darkened screen looked like the one from that kitchen, five years ago.
